chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said:
I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) having been brought a cup of water in which was a handle of silver, so I saw him remove it by his teeth.
ai.seo_question: How did the Imams avoid drinking directly from silver vessels?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of the prohibition (*nah*) against drinking from gold and silver vessels, specifically highlighting the method of avoiding direct contact with the precious metal. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) is shown removing the silver handle (*dubbah*) with his teeth, demonstrating that the prohibition applies to the vessel's material rather than just the liquid itself. This incident is often cited by Shia jurists to discuss the nuances of *istihlak* (consumption) and whether the prohibition is for reverence or ritual purity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam who said,
‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been brought a cup of water in which was a handle of silver, so I saw him<sup>asws</sup> remove it by his<sup>asws</sup> teeth’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindiy from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from ‘ Arnr ibn abu Miqdam who has said the following: “
I saw abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when a bowl of water was brought to him (the Imam) in which there was a patch of silver, removing it with his teeth.’”
